title: Continuous storage did not remove flow and tracer ambiguity in a changing mixed-store model
abstract: We test whether continuous storage across a runoff change removes a known flow and natural tracer ambiguity. For one fully mixed store with a discharge law that can change in time, an exact continuous scale transformation preserves flow and all concentration tracer records from the same initial state. Non-negative liquid loss gives a sharp rate bound. For constant stream and liquid loss coefficients k and ell, a scale increase from 1 to b needs at least log(((k+ell)b-k)/ell)/(k+ell), if no other cap binds. No such increase is possible when reference liquid loss is zero. Two synthetic models start identically, then give the same 30% lower steady runoff and 10% faster recession with different recharge and loss changes. Independent integrations agree within 7e-10 in flow and 1e-10 in concentration. Eight of 21 sampled smooth paths fail the loss constraint. A known storage ratio can remove this transition freedom. This is a theory result, not regional attribution. It requires one mixed store, common liquid concentrations and free changes in model functions. Proof, code, synthetic inputs, negative controls, bounds, aggregate checks and provenance are included.

display.caption: Synthetic models preserve flow and decaying tracer records through a continuous change, while their stores diverge. The lower right panel gives the sharp time bound for a 40% scale increase in a constant-rate example. Rates and forcing are illustrative, not fitted to catchment data.
